census.what: Every function in the derived module offered to the real gate, verdict tallied. The gate decides, not a hand filter.
census.extraction: WHOLE MODULE, one target function: every TYPE table kept intact so all positional ids resolve with no remapping, `globals` cleared, `functions` replaced by the single target. `lower_module_to_lir` takes a func_id and lowers exactly ONE function, so keeping the neighbours costs nothing; the earlier full-module attempt scored 0 PROVEN in the NEXT step, `emit_object_with_trust_ir_globals`, which emits every global and refused on an unrelated `__trust_bytes_0`.
census.everything_attributable: 2,388 = 16 + 0 + 2,372 + 0. No row is this probe's artifact and none is unexplained.
census.zero_refuted_note: The gate never claims a derived body MISCOMPILES. Every non-proven case is Unknown -- outside a modelled fragment -- not a disagreement between spec and emitted bytes. This now holds across THREE independent extractions of the same module, which is what makes it the robust finding here.
census.proven_shape: Fifteen are nullary/scalar-parameter, scalar-return container and sort helpers (2-22 instructions). The SIXTEENTH is `clean_kernel::tc::def_eq::delta::<impl TypeChecker<'_>>::lazy_delta_step_no_consts` -- the first proven body that is actually in the typechecker. It appears only once the module is complete, which retracts the earlier 'the smallvec Array::size family and siblings' shape note.
census.is_zero_verdict: Unknown { reason: "lower_module_to_lir failed: function `clean_kernel::level::Level::is_zero` has an `Undef` that is not a provably-dead memory-merge seed: Undef value 15 is not consumed by a single Store into a local Alloca" } -- the crystal's DESIGNATED width-one target, refused by this gate in this O3-derived module, in the producer class. The probe reports this body's verdict verbatim wherever it lands.
census.axis_is_asserted: The probe asserts cls_total == unknown and proven+refuted+unknown+holes == 2,388. The first published axis summed to 2,371 against 2,372 because the `is_zero` arm incremented the verdict tally and not the class rollup; the assertions now stand where that arithmetic was.
census.axis_finding_RETRACTED: 674 of 2,372 (28%) are PRODUCER gaps -- rustc knows those layouts and the extractor did not record them, and the `Undef`s are values the producer emitted. Neither needs an IR format change or a spec change, which is the opposite of what the retracted 'types dominate' reading implied. 361 of the 551 are one type: `core::option::Option`. The one claim that survives all three readings is that OPCODES ARE A ROUNDING ERROR: 45 of 2,372.
census.axis_finding_retraction: The sentence above -- '675 of 2,372 (28%) are PRODUCER gaps ... neither needs an IR format change or a spec change' -- is RETRACTED as to its implication, measured the same day at trust `9aa4f5856b`. The CLASSIFICATION holds: those bodies really do refuse first on a datum the producer never recorded. The IMPLICATION does not. Stamping a synthetic layout onto all 175 layout-less structs clears every one of the 551 refusals and moves PROVEN by ZERO (16 -> 16); they refuse one step later, with 'aggregate field outside the scalar C-layout slice' going 385 -> 867 (+482). The layout datum is NECESSARY and nowhere near SUFFICIENT. Behind all 551 is the CONVERTER's aggregate fragment, so the producer fix buys a different refusal message and not one proved body.
census.what_the_axis_is_for: A census reports each body's FIRST refusal, and the first refusal is not the binding one. The axis is an accurate map of where bodies stop; it is NOT a ranking of levers. To size a lever, measure the DELTA in PROVEN when that refusal is removed -- which is what the what-if does, and what turned the largest-looking producer bucket into a zero.
census.binding_constraint: The CONVERTER's type/aggregate fragment, and it is reached before anything else. For `infer_type` itself the refused type is Struct(2) = `core::result::Result` spelled ["__tag","__v0_0","__v1_0"] with size None. The three types blocking the whole TypeChecker family: `datatype::clean_kernel::expr::Expr` (opaque, 0 fields, 30 bodies), flat `core::option::Option` (25), flat `core::result::Result` (17). The 'refused at its SIGNATURE' reading carried until 2026-09-16 pointed the work at the gate's obligation; widening the obligation would move nothing, because the converter never produces a LIR to hand it. It does NOT follow that the obligation would accept an aggregate return once the converter is widened -- nothing reaches it, so that is untested.
census.enum_layout_inconsistency: Localized while measuring the above and real regardless of its value as a lever: `lower_enum_adt` (trust-mir-extract ty_convert.rs:3602) sets `layout: None` while filling `enum_layout`, so an enum reaches the bridge TWICE -- as an EnumDef with a full descriptor (109 of 117 enums here; `core::option::Option` at size 8/16/24/88/144/496 across instantiations) and as a flattened StructDef `["__tag","__v1_0"]` with no layout. 361 of the 551 name that flattened Option. The datum is in the module, on the other table.
census.three_blockers_are_one: `lower_enum_adt` (ty_convert.rs:3602) renders an enum as a flat `__tag`/`__v` struct with `layout: None`. That single producer decision is what the converter's TYPE fragment refuses (the 'signature' story), what the memory-layout path refuses (the 551 'no recorded size/align'), and what the aggregate slice refuses behind it. Three separately-documented blockers, one object.

bottom_of_link5.what: The refusal chain followed to the end. It bottoms out in a def-path-gated producer decision about the kernel's own central type, not in the gate, the converter, or the bridge.
chain: obligation: never reached (2,360 of 2,388 bodies stop before it)
converter: unsupported type in `function return`: Struct(StructId(2))
both are Ty::Datatype, which carries NO LAYOUT by construction
ty_convert.rs:1907-1931 routes Level, ExprKind and Expr to Datatype BY DEF PATH
because the layout-bearing Ty::Adt rendering OOM-killed extraction at ~464 MB (recorded in source at ty_convert.rs:1919; not re-measured here)
bottom_of_link5.not_fixable_downstream: Not in the converter (no size -> no ABI class). Not in the bridge (the single-variant Datatype expansion buys field identity, never layout; the expanded def still has size None). Not by re-spelling as Ty::Enum (refused by the same fragment). map_scalar_int_ty accepts exactly {i8..i128, isize/usize, char, bool, Ptr, Func}.
bottom_of_link5.RETRACTED_what_it_would_take: The explosion is a property of `trust_types::Ty`, the producer's INTERMEDIATE representation, not of the target IR -- trust_ir's module format is an id table, inherently finite for recursive types AND layout-bearing (109 of 117 enums here carry a full EnumLayoutDescriptor). A representation with by-name refs carrying layout would be both. That is a `trust_types::Ty` change = THE WIRE BREAK ALREADY SCOPED FOR PROGRAMMES D AND E (Ty not #[non_exhaustive], 2,893 mentions, binary.rs VERSION 29, four repos). Those were carried as separate optional programmes; they are on the CRITICAL PATH for link 5 of this goal, and nothing smaller reaches it.
bottom_of_link5.retraction: The 'what it would take' above -- the trust_types::Ty representation change (D/E wire break), 'nothing smaller reaches it' -- is WITHDRAWN, measured. Stamping a layout onto every layout-less struct leaves the refusal BYTE-IDENTICAL ('unsupported type in `function return`: Struct(StructId(2))') and does not move the stage distribution at all (2360/12/16 both sides). The layout is never consulted there: `map_scalar_int_ty` matches on the Ty CONSTRUCTOR. The D/E wire break is NOT established as on link 5's critical path.

three_walls.1_converter_signature_fragment: map_scalar_int_ty (module_to_lir.rs:356) admits exactly {i8..i128, isize/usize, char, bool, Ptr, Func} and refuses every aggregate BY CONSTRUCTOR -- layout-independent. Stops infer_type, 205 of 206 impl TypeChecker bodies, 2,360 of 2,388. ONE function, ONE crate. FIRST.
three_walls.2_obligation_is_a_scalar_return_equality: trust_ir_function_semantics requires func_ty.returns.len()==1 (:696) and one out_width from signature_reg_width(returns[0]) (:702); SpecSemantics carries a single value:Formula at a single width. REAL, and SECOND -- which makes the 2026-09-15 design note right about the work and wrong only about which step refuses first.
three_walls.3_unknown: Nothing reaches far enough to say. No claim made.

bottom_of_link5.not_a_blocker: The TARGET IR: trust_cg_lower::types::Type already has Struct(Vec<Type>), Array(Box<Type>,u32) and Enum{tag_width,variants}. LIR can represent an aggregate return today.
bottom_of_link5.module_is_exhausted: Twelve bodies reach the obligation and are refused THERE -- the only candidates for a proved body needing no aggregate work. ALL TWELVE are deliberate fail-closed walls: 4 the same aggregate wall on the spec side (Enum 54/89/33), 2 the move-only pointer fragment, 2 unit returns ('expected exactly 1 return value, got 0' -- correctly refused, since discharging a vacuous obligation is what the vacuity firewall exists to stop), 2 Alloca, 1 Load. So 16 proved is what this fragment yields on this module and there is no residue of accidental refusals to harvest.
bottom_of_link5.walls_1_and_2_are_one_job: module_to_lir.rs constructs ZERO aggregate LIR types (I64 63, I8 14, I128 9, I32 8, I16 6, B1 5; no Struct/Array/Enum), while mapping.rs and lower.rs in the same crate do build LirType::Struct. The gate's converter is scalar-only BY CONSTRUCTION because the obligation is a scalar register equality -- co-designed. So widening wall 1 alone is not merely worth zero proved bodies, it is NOT COHERENT: there is no aggregate value model to put in a signature. Cheapest coherent slice: the 583 returns <=16 bytes, where wall 2 widens from one register to two.

RETIRED_module_does_not_model_expr.finding: CATEGORICAL. Walking infer_type's return: Struct(2) Result -> .__tag Isize (scalar), .__v0_0 Struct(0) datatype::Expr OPAQUE 0 fields, .__v1_0 Struct(1) datatype::TypeError OPAQUE 0 fields. Every path reaches an opaque leaf in ONE step. The expanded Expr does not help: Struct(220).kind is Struct(101) ExprKind with ZERO fields. The whole Expr/ExprKind/Level/TypeError cluster carries no structure.
RETIRED_module_does_not_model_expr.why_it_ends_the_converter_line: Not 'has no layout' -- has no content. The gate proves the return VALUE equals what the machine leaves, which needs the module to MODEL that value. An opaque zero-field def is a havoc symbol. Widening map_scalar_int_ty, widening the obligation, supplying a layout -- none give the spec side a value, and an obligation with an unconstrained symbol on both sides is VACUOUS, which the vacuity firewall refuses. The three walls are real and all DOWNSTREAM of this for infer_type.
RETIRED_module_does_not_model_expr.deliberate: ty_convert.rs:1907-1931 routes Level/ExprKind/Expr to Ty::Datatype by def path; lower_adt_as_datatype renders recursive children as BY-NAME refs -- the by-name ref IS the opacity, a cut point so the cluster stays finitely declarable (source comment :1919: the Ty::Adt rendering OOM-killed extraction at ~464 MB). A designed refusal, like the atomic quarantine.
RETIRED_module_does_not_model_expr.what_completion_requires: An AUTHORED MODEL of the opaque type -- the shape link 4 already executed for Level::is_zero, where ir_lzb_module is the derived function plus an authored model of the one callee rustc could not give a body for, deref carried as a labelled ASSUMPTION with its residual named. Link 5 for infer_type needs an authored `Expr` model on that pattern: spec-side work in clean-verify, NOT converter work in trust-cg-bridge.
RETIRED_module_does_not_model_expr.RETIRED: True OF THE MODULE and still binds any body that CONSTRUCTS an Expr. NOT the binding constraint for infer_type, whose ok path TRANSPORTS its return (block 5: Call infer_type_fast; Store; block 3: Load; Return -- the Expr is moved, never inspected). Stated as categorical, it was too strong.

measured_distance_to_a_proved_infer_type.target_is_smaller_than_the_precedent: infer_type blocks=6 instructions=36 calls=2; level::Level::is_zero blocks=17 instructions=52 calls=6. Link 4 closed for is_zero with ~1,790 lines of spec. infer_type's BODY is the small part.
measured_distance_to_a_proved_infer_type.transport_vs_construct: infer_type's ok path TRANSPORTS its return (Call infer_type_fast -> Store -> Load -> Return; the Expr is never inspected). A body that CONSTRUCTS an Expr needs its internals modelled; one that TRANSPORTS it does not -- the obligation is that the bytes move, which a miscompile falsifies and which is not vacuous.
measured_distance_to_a_proved_infer_type.deepest_wall_is_the_call_method: The converter inlines pure leaf calls to a fixpoint and fail-closes on the residue -- a whole-function call-free method with NO compositional call rule. A recursive cycle cannot be inlined.
measured_distance_to_a_proved_infer_type.cut_set_has_size_one: All 12 back edges are heartbeat_profiler sort code (quicksort, median3_rec, drift::sort) reached through tick_heartbeat -- NONE is infer_type's own typechecking recursion. Cutting that one callee makes the closure acyclic. Cutting a callee with an authored model is exactly ir_lzb_deref for is_zero.
what_stands_between_here_and_a_proved_in: 1. an authored `tick_heartbeat` model -- the cut making the closure acyclic; harder than the deref model because it MUTATES a counter (a state obligation, not a read)
2. wall 1: map_scalar_int_ty refuses every aggregate by constructor; applies to all 113
3. wall 2: the obligation is a scalar-return equality (returns.len()==1, one out_width)
4. the error path's live `Undef`s -- the derived body builds Err(undefined) where real Rust constructs a TypeError; same class that refuses is_zero here; a producer-fidelity gap
measured_distance_to_a_proved_infer_type.not_established: That 7,379 instructions actually inline (only that no CYCLE forbids it; still ~95x the precedent), or that walls 1-2 fall once they do.

why_no_widening_moves_the_number.finding: The gate's fragment is a CONJUNCTION of seven narrow axes. 17 bodies violate 0 axes (the fragment's entire population), 61 violate exactly 1, and 2,310 -- 97% -- violate two or more.
why_no_widening_moves_the_number.why_16_never_moved: 16 of the 17 bodies that clear all seven axes already prove. The fragment's population is exhausted; every widening this module admits is a two-axis job at minimum. The 61 single-axis bodies split five ways, so the BEST single widening reaches 27.
why_no_widening_moves_the_number.three_widenings_all_zero: supply the missing struct layout (16->16, measured); admit aggregate returns (incoherent -- no aggregate value model in the converter); admit scalar-newtype returns (21 signatures newly map, but those bodies carry Load 93, Store 106, Alloca 54, Call 50, Undef 89).
why_no_widening_moves_the_number.CALIBRATION: infer_type violates 5 of 7 axes (signature, call, memory, undef, aggregate ops). level::Level::is_zero -- the crystal's COMPLETED width-one chain -- violates 4 of 7 (call, memory, undef, borrow) and is NOT inside this gate's fragment either. So this gate is not the instrument by which that chain closed, and holding infer_type to it sets a bar the precedent never met. Whether 'link 5 for infer_type' means THIS gate or the route is_zero took is an OWNER question; every 'how far is infer_type' number in this repo, including all of 2026-09-16's, implicitly answers the stronger one without saying so.
